questions.question: Why is TCP considered a connection-oriented protocol?

answers.a: It does not require an initial handshake.
answers.b: It ensures data is delivered in sequence and without errors.
answers.c: It does not retransmit lost packets.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the three-way handshake in TCP?

answers.a: To verify the receiver's IP address.
answers.b: To establish a reliable connection before data transfer.
answers.c: To encrypt the data being transmitted.

questions.question: What happens when a TCP sender detects packet loss?

answers.a: It reduces the congestion window size.
answers.d: It ignores the loss and continues sending.

questions.question: What is the main difference between Go-Back-N and Selective Repeat protocols?

answers.a: Go-Back-N retransmits all packets after a loss, while Selective Repeat only retransmits lost packets.
answers.b: Go-Back-N does not use acknowledgments, while Selective Repeat does.
answers.c: Go-Back-N allows unlimited packet transmission, while Selective Repeat does not.
answers.d: Go-Back-N requires TCP, while Selective Repeat does not.
